{"path":"DESIGN-SYSTEM.md","content":"# Design system: Godzilla 1.0.0 Godzilla is the design system for RIFT CMS documentation sites — born from the rift where molten content rises to the surface. Warm volcanic neutrals, magma-orange accents, and a dense, link-heavy, code-heavy layout language built for technical docs (Astro-style hub/detail pages, left navigation, API reference tables, and syntax-styled code blocks). Every page on this site is built from these components and tokens. Use them rather than writing custom markup or styling — hand-rolled equivalents break visual consistency and will not pick up future design-system changes. ## Components ### alert Callout box for notes, warnings, and danger/breaking-change notices inside docs content. | Parameter | Type | Default | Description | |---|---|---|---| | `variant` | string | `info` | One of info, success, warning, danger. | | `title` | string | `Note` | Callout heading. | | `body_html` | html | `This endpoint is deprecated in favor of ` | Callout body content, may include inline links. | **Usage:** variant must match one of the fixed CSS suffixes: info, success, warning, danger. Any other value falls back to the default neutral alert border. ### card Link tile used on hub pages to point at guides, API endpoints, SDKs, or concepts. | Parameter | Type | Default | Description | |---|---|---|---| | `href` | string | `/guides/building-your-first-pipeline` | Destination URL. | | `tag` | string | `Guide` | Short category label shown above the title. | | `title` | string | `Building your first pipeline` | Card title. | | `description` | string | `Learn how to assemble your first data pi` | One or two sentence summary. | **Usage:** Use one card component call per tile on hub/index pages such as Guides hub, API Reference hub, and SDKs hub. ### chip Small inline badge used for version tags and status labels (e.g. v2, Beta, Deprecated). | Parameter | Type | Default | Description | |---|---|---|---| | `label` | string | `v2` | Chip text. | | `variant` | string | `primary` | One of primary, success, warning, danger, info, or omit for neutral. | **Usage:** variant maps directly to a fixed CSS class suffix; unknown values render as the neutral default chip style. ### code-block Syntax-styled code block with filename/language header and copy affordance, used throughout guides and API reference pages. | Parameter | Type | Default | Description | |---|---|---|---| | `filename` | string | `pipeline.config.json` | Optional filename or example label shown in the header. | | `language` | string | `json` | Language label shown top-right. | | `code` | html | `{ "pipeline": "ingest-orders" }` | The pre-formatted code content (already escaped/highlighted markup if needed). | **Usage:** code is inserted verbatim inside a pre/code block; author it as plain text or pre-escaped markup, since there is no runtime syntax highlighter in this template. ### docs-pagination Prev/next page navigation shown at the bottom of docs content. | Parameter | Type | Default | Description | |---|---|---|---| | `prev_href` | string | `/getting-started/installation` | URL of previous page. | | `prev_label` | string | `Installation` | Title of previous page. | | `next_href` | string | `/getting-started/authentication` | URL of next page. | | `next_label` | string | `Authentication` | Title of next page. | **Usage:** Place once at the bottom of any sequential docs page (Getting Started, Guides, API Reference, SDKs). ### docs-toc On-this-page table of contents rendered alongside long docs content. | Parameter | Type | Default | Description | |---|---|---|---| | `items_html` | html | `

{"path":"llms.txt","content":"# Godzilla Docs

> Everything you need to build data pipelines on the Godzilla platform.

## Pages
- [Changelog](https://localhost:3002/changelog): Recent changes to the Godzilla API and platform.
- [Concepts](https://localhost:3002/concepts): The core building blocks of Godzilla: pipelines, connectors, events, and schemas.
- [Connectors](https://localhost:3002/concepts-connectors): What a connector is in Godzilla: a pre-built integration to a source or destination system, with its own auth and catalog of built-in types.
- [Events](https://localhost:3002/concepts-events): What an event is in Godzilla: the atomic unit of data moving through a pipeline, plus the platform's own lifecycle events.
- [Glossary](https://localhost:3002/glossary): Definitions for Godzilla's core terms, each linking to its full explanation.
- [Godzilla Docs](https://localhost:3002/index): Everything you need to build data pipelines on the Godzilla platform.
- [Migration guide (v1 → v2)](https://localhost:3002/migration-guide-v1-to-v2): Move an existing v1 integration to the v2 API: cursor pagination, webhooks, and the new error shape.
- [Pipelines](https://localhost:3002/concepts-pipelines): What a pipeline is in Godzilla: a named, versioned workflow that moves data from a source connector through transform steps to a destination.
- [Release notes archive](https://localhost:3002/release-notes-archive): Older v1-era release notes, superseded by the current changelog.
- [Schemas](https://localhost:3002/concepts-schemas): How event payload shapes are declared, validated, and evolved in Godzilla.
- [Security & compliance overview](https://localhost:3002/security-and-compliance): How Godzilla handles data in transit and at rest, credential storage, and compliance posture.
- [Support / Contact](https://localhost:3002/support): How to reach the Godzilla team for support, sales, or security reports.
- [Troubleshooting / FAQ](https://localhost:3002/troubleshooting): Common problems and fixes across pipelines, connectors, and webhooks.

## api
- [API Reference](https://localhost:3002/api/index): The Godzilla v2 REST API: pipelines, connectors, events, webhooks, and rate limits.
- [Connectors endpoint](https://localhost:3002/api/connectors): Create, list, and rotate credentials for connectors via the v2 REST API.
- [Events endpoint](https://localhost:3002/api/events): Query and replay events that have flowed through a pipeline via the v2 REST API.
- [Pipelines endpoint](https://localhost:3002/api/pipelines): Create, list, and manage pipelines via the v2 REST API.
- [Quotas & billing](https://localhost:3002/api/quotas-billing): Plan tiers, workspace resource limits, overage behavior, and billing policies.
- [Limits, quotas & errors](https://localhost:3002/api/rate-limits-errors): Standard-tier rate limits, pagination envelope, and the v2 API's error response shape.
- [Transforms endpoint](https://localhost:3002/api/transforms): Create and list transform steps within pipelines via the v2 REST API.
- [Webhooks endpoint](https://localhost:3002/api/webhooks): Subscribe to Godzilla platform lifecycle events over outbound HTTP via the v2 REST API.

## getting-started
- [Authentication](https://localhost:3002/getting-started/authentication): Authenticate API requests with a bearer API key.
- [Getting Started](https://localhost:3002/getting-started/index): Everything you need to get up and running with Godzilla data pipelines.
- [Installation](https://localhost:3002/getting-started/installation): Install the Godzilla SDK or start calling the REST API directly.
- [Quickstart](https://localhost:3002/getting-started/quickstart): Go from zero to a running pipeline in five minutes.

## guides
- [Building your first pipeline](https://localhost:3002/guides/building-your-first-pipeline): Create a source connector, a destination connector, and the pipeline that connects them, end to end.
- [Connecting a data source]

Migration guide (v1 → v2) v1 retired

v1 reached end of life on 2026-08-01 alongside the webhooks GA changelog entry. This guide covers the three breaking changes you need to handle to move a v1 integration to v2.

1. Pagination: offset → cursor

v1 used page/per_page query parameters. v2 uses an opaque cursor and next_cursor — see Limits, quotas & errors for the exact envelope.

diff diff 
- GET /v1/pipelines?page=2&per_page=20
+ GET /v2/pipelines?cursor=eyJvZmZzZXQiOjIwfQ

2. Status checks: polling → webhooks

v1 had no push notifications — you polled a pipeline's status endpoint. v2 replaces this with the Webhooks endpoint: subscribe to pipeline.completed and pipeline.failed instead of polling.

3. Error shape

v1 returned bare error strings. v2 wraps every error in an object with a stable code field. Update any error handling that matched on message text — see the error shape reference.

v1 is retired

v1 endpoints no longer accept requests. If you're seeing 404s on /v1/* paths, that's why — there is no grace-period fallback.

Still stuck?

Common migration issues are covered in Troubleshooting / FAQ.

Webhooks endpoint v2

Subscribe to platform lifecycle events — such as pipeline.completed or connector.error — as outbound HTTP requests to a URL you control. This is the v2 replacement for v1's polling-only status checks; see the Migration guide if you're moving off v1.

Create a webhook subscription

POST /v2/webhooks

Name Type Required Description
typestringYesHTTPS endpoint Godzilla will POST events to.
eventsarrayYesList of event types to subscribe to, e.g. [\"pipeline.failed\"].
secretstringNoShared secret used to sign the X-Godzilla-Signature header. Auto-generated if omitted.
webhook-payload.json json 
{\n  \"id\": \"evt_wh_2091\",\n  \"type\": \"pipeline.failed\",\n  \"occurred_at\": \"2026-08-18T09:14:02Z\",\n  \"data\": { \"pipeline_id\": \"pl_ingest_orders\", \"error\": \"destination_timeout\" }\n}
Verify the signature

Always verify X-Godzilla-Signature before trusting a webhook payload. Unsigned or unverifiable requests to your endpoint should be rejected, not processed.

Delivery retries

A webhook delivery that doesn't receive a 2xx response is retried with exponential backoff for up to 24 hours, then marked failed. Failed deliveries are visible per-subscription and can be manually redelivered.

Pipelines

A pipeline is the core unit of work in Godzilla: a named, versioned data-processing workflow that moves data from a source connector, through zero or more transform steps, to a destination connector. Every pipeline runs as a sequence of events flowing through that path.

Anatomy of a pipeline

Every pipeline has three parts:

  • Source — the connector that emits events into the pipeline (a database, a queue, an upload, a webhook).
  • Transforms — an ordered list of steps that reshape, filter, or enrich events as they pass through. Transforms are optional; a pipeline with none is a pass-through copy.
  • Destination — the connector that events are written to once transforms complete.
Pipelines are declarative

You describe the desired source, transforms, and destination; Godzilla schedules and retries the runs. You never manage worker processes directly.

Pipeline state

A pipeline is always in one of three states:

  • draft — configured but not yet processing events.
  • active — running on its configured schedule or trigger.
  • paused — temporarily stopped; resumes from the last checkpoint.

Versioning

Pipeline configuration is versioned. Publishing a new version does not affect events already in flight on the previous version — in-flight runs finish on the version they started on. This matters most when a pipeline definition is part of a larger migration; see the Migration guide for an example of retiring an old pipeline version safely.

Connectors

A connector is a pre-built integration to an external system that a Pipeline reads from or writes to. Connectors handle authentication, batching, and retry behavior for a specific system so pipeline authors don't have to.

Connector direction

  • Source — emits events into a pipeline (e.g. a change-data-capture stream from Postgres).

  • Bidirectional — a small set of connectors, like the generic Webhook connector, can act as either.

Built-in connector catalog

Rotating connector credentials

Rotating a connector's credentials pauses any pipeline using it for the duration of the rotation. Plan credential rotations outside peak processing windows.

Connector health

Each connector reports a health status independent of any single pipeline: healthy, degraded, or down. A connector shared across multiple pipelines only needs to be fixed once — every pipeline referencing it recovers automatically.

A schema defines the structural contract for an event's payload. While Godzilla enforces a standard top-level event envelope, schemas declare the exact data types, required properties, and value constraints of the user payload inside each event.

Declaring event payload shapes

Schemas in Godzilla use standard JSON Schema (draft-07) specifications. Each schema maps to an event type and declares what fields must be present and what data formats they must follow.

{\n  \"$schema\": \"http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#\",\n  \"title\": \"OrderCreatedPayload\",\n  \"type\": \"object\",\n  \"required\": [\"order_id\", \"customer_id\", \"amount_cents\", \"currency\"],\n  \"properties\": {\n    \"order_id\": {\n      \"type\": \"string\",\n      \"pattern\": \"^ord_[a-zA-Z0-9]+$\"\n    },\n    \"customer_id\": {\n      \"type\": \"string\"\n    },\n    \"amount_cents\": {\n      \"type\": \"integer\",\n      \"minimum\": 0\n    },\n    \"currency\": {\n      \"type\": \"string\",\n      \"enum\": [\"USD\", \"EUR\", \"GBP\", \"CAD\"]\n    },\n    \"metadata\": {\n      \"type\": \"object\"\n    }\n  },\n  \"additionalProperties\": false\n}

Payload validation lifecycle

Validation runs automatically as data moves through a pipeline:

  1. Source ingestion: When a source connector emits an event, Godzilla matches the event's type against the registered schema and validates the payload.
  2. Transform boundaries: After each transform step that alters payload structures, the output can be re-validated before continuing down the pipeline.
  3. Destination write: Ensures only schema-compliant events reach destination sinks (such as Snowflake or PostgreSQL).
Validation occurs at runtime

Schema enforcement happens at event ingestion before expensive transforms or downstream writes occur. Malformed payloads are trapped early, protecting downstream systems from invalid state.

Validation modes

Pipelines can configure one of three validation modes depending on your data guarantees:

Mode Behavior on valid payload Behavior on invalid payload
strict Processed through pipeline Rejected immediately; event is moved to the dead-letter queue
permissive Processed through pipeline Processed with a validation_warning attribute attached and metric incremented
disabled Processed through pipeline Bypasses payload validation checks completely

Handling validation failures

When an event fails validation under strict mode, Godzilla emits a validation.failed error, cancels downstream processing for that event, and routes it to the pipeline's dead-letter queue. The dead-lettered record includes detailed validation diagnostics:

  • failing_path — the JSON pointer to the invalid field (e.g. /payload/amount_cents).
  • constraint — the rule that failed (e.g. minimum or required).
  • received_value — the actual invalid value received.

To inspect and replay failed events after correcting schema definitions or source data, see the Error handling & recovery guide and the Events replay endpoint.

Schema versioning and evolution

Event schemas evolve as your application grows. Godzilla supports backwards-compatible schema changes without downtime:

  • Additive changes: Adding optional fields or expanding enum values are non-breaking and can be deployed without updating existing event consumers.
  • Breaking changes: Adding required fields, removing fields, or changing data types require publishing a new schema version (e.g. order.created.v2) or applying a transform. See Transforming events in flight for reshaping payloads during migrations.

  • Pipelines — configuring validation modes and routing rules on pipelines.
  • Transforming events in flight — reshaping event payloads to match destination schemas.

My pipeline isn't processing events

Walk through Error handling & recovery — it covers both diagnosing the failure and replaying events once fixed.

I'm not receiving webhook deliveries

I'm getting 429s

You've hit the standard-tier limit described in Limits, quotas & errors. Back off using the Retry-After header, or review Quotas & billing if your workload needs higher plan tier limits or customized throughput.

Migrating from v1?

A number of "it worked yesterday" reports trace back to v1's offset pagination or polling patterns carried over into v2 code. See the Migration guide.
